substantive_reconstruction.function_carrier_and_root: The same C2 sign character on C is a valid finite unitary irreducible action here. Cubing commutes with multiplication by either sign and is entire, but equality f=lambda I would force lambda=1 at z=1 and then fail at z=2. Thus the additional old field/dimension conditions do not fix functional equivariance. A nonlinear function has no endomorphism matrix or characteristic polynomial for this purpose. In the corrected branch f lies explicitly in End_F(V). For n=dim_F V>0, det(tI-f) is monic of degree n, so algebraic closure produces a root lambda. In finite-dimensional linear algebra its zero determinant means a nonzero kernel vector for lambda I-f. Positive finite dimension supplies both the nonconstant polynomial and the matrix singularity criterion; algebraic closure supplies a root. The candidate separates these roles accurately.
substantive_reconstruction.shift_and_irreducibility: For h=f-lambda I, linearity of f and the identity gives h in End_F(V). Since each phi(g) is F-linear, it commutes with scalar multiplication; combining that with f phi(g)=phi(g)f proves h phi(g)=phi(g)h in the displayed order. The eigenvector v is nonzero and h(v)=0. Linearity makes the kernel a vector subspace, and this intertwining relation makes it invariant. Algebraic irreducibility then forces that nonzero kernel to be V, hence h=0. This is also the zero-or-isomorphism lemma with its invertible alternative ruled out. No circular scalar-Schur premise is used to prove the shift is scalar, and no polynomial is assigned to the nonlinear discriminator.
substantive_reconstruction.commutant_and_zero_space: Inside End_F(V), every X commuting with all action maps satisfies the same proved hypotheses and is scalar; conversely linearity of the action proves every lambda I commutes. These are both inclusions of the claimed set equality, not an unsupported appeal to the word commutant. For nonzero V, evaluating (lambda-mu)I at a nonzero vector proves uniqueness of the scalar, so F I has dimension one. For V=0, all endomorphisms and the identity are the zero operator; every lambda represents it, and F I is zero-dimensional. The set equality still holds but there is no eigenvector or scalar uniqueness. The candidate handles that branch separately if the adopted definition permits zero irreducibles, which the source's literal invariant-subspace definition does not explicitly exclude.
substantive_reconstruction.real_field_boundary: I checked the real C4 example without importing complex irreducibility. Its generator J=[[0,-1],[1,0]] is orthogonal and has J^2=-I. A proper nonzero real invariant subspace of R^2 would be a line, so for its generator v one would have Jv=a v with real a. Squaring gives a^2=-1, impossible. This proves real irreducibility. Yet J is a non-real-scalar real-linear operator commuting with all powers of itself. The example truly shows failure of the unrestricted scalar conclusion when algebraic closure is removed; finite group, finite dimension and orthogonality alone do not replace it. It is not a complex irreducibility counterexample, since complexifying creates eigenlines.
substantive_reconstruction.infinite_dimension_boundary: For K=C(t), each multiplication by g in K^times is an invertible C-linear operator on V=K, defining the stated algebraic representation. Powers 1,t,t^2,... are linearly independent, proving infinite dimension. If a nonzero invariant complex-linear W contains w nonzero, then for every v nonzero the allowed group element v/w carries w to v. Hence W=K: this is genuinely irreducible, unlike a reducible trivial-action example. Multiplication T by t commutes with all g and is not a complex scalar; for each lambda in C, T-lambda I has inverse multiplication by 1/(t-lambda), so T has no complex eigenvalue. This is a valid boundary outside finite dimension while retaining an algebraically closed base. No topology, Hilbert norm, boundedness or compact-group continuity is supplied for K^times, so it cannot refute separately hypothesized topological/unitary Schur variants.
